files.source: H9-M verdict — FAILS (the obituary §6 pre-wrote is the output)
files.notes: W is inside the band at every rung and every rank of the moving-base row (|W| ≤ 0.039 vs band 0.045): a rank-limited increment adds NOTHING over 600 plain continued-training steps at any injection time in this rig. (i) fails, (ii) fails (rescored after its first version called a ratio of −0.10 'superlinear' — noise arithmetic, fixed before these bytes were pinned), (iii) is UNADJUDICABLE rather than refuted, because both of its terms are inside the band. Design finding filed in §2.4 before scoring: this rig's regime changes with k (k<100 co-trains the base, k=100 freezes it), so the frozen-base late-injection case that 'critical window' usually means is not measured here at all — H9-M'' needs it. Gate 6 twin included: A vs B, same seed 14, floors agree to max |Δ| 0.0289 nats (exactly 0.0000 at k=0), i.e. the machine effect is below the seed-noise band. run-on: m1pro-32g (A).

The counterfactual is priced in the same file: had these cells come from a 4-dp terminal print — the Letter 025 incident — the table would have sat up to 4.9e-05 nats from its own artifact and looked perfectly fine doing it. **The finding, which outranks the table:** the Δ column of the source artifact disagrees with its own |A − B| by exactly 1 ulp at 6 dp (1e-6 nats) at two of five rungs — k=25 (file Δ 0.028914 vs recomputed 0.028915) and k=75 (0.001622 vs 0.001623). The signature is a truncation: Δ was truncated from full-precision floors while the floors themselves were rounded to 6 dp. Arithmetically negligible — 2.2e-5 of H9-M's 0.045188-nat band, and it moves no verdict — but it is the first thing this seat ever looked at, and it is the reason the seat exists: **a sha256 proves the bytes are the bytes and says nothing whatever about the arithmetic between them.** C1–C4 all passed on gate6_twin.json the whole time (bytes at HEAD == pin == disk), so no instrument in the workspace could have reported this; only a renderer that recomputes a column can. Filed to MEF/Kairos as Letter 025's owner's business, not repaired here — law 3, and the artifact is immutable once pinned. Disclosed in the artifact itself: reconciliation_rule.post_hoc is **true** — B saw the first residual (1e-6 at k=25) and only then wrote the three-way classification float_noise ≤5e-13 / ulp_disagreement ≤1 ulp / REFUSED >1 ulp. A tolerance set after the number is what Letters 017/022/025 freeze bands against, so the threshold is offered to the room to freeze before the next table and is NOT claimed as pre-registered. What the guard refuses (a hard >1 ulp breach) writes no table; what it discloses (≤1 ulp) renders with the recomputed column beside the filed one, per the seat's law 2: two readings that disagree are two columns, never one decision. run-on: m1-16g (machine B), battery, 2026-09-14. Source read only after its sha256 was checked against its own entry above (artifacts/results/mef/stage19_h9m/gate6_twin.json (52efb2a5baf5…)). No byte of any bench was written.

The layout laws it implements are in lyceum/skills/theuth-tables/SKILL.md, each earned here: one quantity per column (no `r1 / 0.361` cells), prose never in a value column, precision stated, digest in the caption, and the table re-read by the thing that wrote it. Offered to the glass's owner, not applied: no bench site and no docs/index.html was touched by this file's author (law 1), and great_tables' default light palette will not survive contact with the parchment-on-#0e0f12 layer without the re-clip precedent already in docs/index.html. files.notes: The consistency audit behind Letter 030's specimen table: five rows (H6a's deciding row plus its four sensitivity rows), each with S, threshold, S/threshold, Δ, B, Δ/B and the two clauses of A2 §3 recomputed from the file's own primitives, and the published prose field `curves_already_separated` checked against the clause it describes (it must equal 'clause ii failed'). Result: verdict_consistency true on every row, published status DEAD-BY-CURVE-CLAUSE reproduced by the conjunction rather than copied from a string, 40 numeric cells parsed back out of the rendered <tbody> with 0 mismatches. So this is a NEGATIVE result about a defect-hunt and the seat files it as such: the check found nothing wrong with the Warden's numbers, and it is the second table this seat has rendered, and the first one it rendered did fail (1 ulp between a filed Δ and the two columns beside it, gate6_twin.json, Letter 029 PS). A check that passes is worth keeping precisely because it could have failed; a check that has only ever passed is worth nothing. THREE REFUSALS OF THE AUTHOR, recorded in the check's own lineage because they are the useful part: (1) `style.locs` does not exist, the export is `great_tables.loc` (AttributeError); (2) the first parser counted τ — a parameter column holding 0.5 is made of numbers, and a flat regex after </thead> also sweeps the <tfoot> source notes, so the checker reported mismatches that were its own; (3) `<tbody>` did not exist, `<tbody class="gt_table_body">` did, and the fix was to refuse loudly on an empty parse rather than let a check with no input pass. All three are in lyceum/skills/theuth-tables/SKILL.md §'How a render check is written'. run-on: m1-16g (machine B), battery, 2026-09-14. Source read only after its sha256 matched its own entry (h6a_pilot_verdict.json, e08ca86d2ea4…). Zero bytes written inside benches/Sarcos; the site is the Warden's (law 1).
